instruction: Determine how many files in '/tmp/test_files' were changed within the last 20 to 40 days, then save this number to '/tmp/file_count.txt'.

parameters.command: mkdir -p /tmp/test_files/data && touch /tmp/test_files/data/old1.txt /tmp/test_files/data/old2.log /tmp/test_files/data/target1.txt /tmp/test_files/data/target2.txt /tmp/test_files/data/target3.dat /tmp/test_files/data/recent.txt && find /tmp/test_files/data -name 'old*' -exec touch -d '50 days ago' {} \; && find /tmp/test_files/data -name 'target*' -exec touch -d '30 days ago' {} \; && touch -d '5 days ago' /tmp/test_files/data/recent.txt

command: import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'alt', 't'); time.sleep(0.5)

result.command: bash -c 'if [ -f "/tmp/file_count.txt" ]; then count=$(cat /tmp/file_count.txt | tr -d "\n\r " 2>/dev/null); if [ "$count" = "3" ]; then echo "Success: The task was completed correctly."; else echo "Failure: Count is $count but expected 3"; fi; else echo "Failure: File /tmp/file_count.txt does not exist"; fi'

include: Success: The task was completed correctly.

metadata.explanation: Task variation that requires finding and counting files modified in a specific date range (20-40 days ago) and saving the count to a file. Setup creates: old1/2 (50 days ago - outside range), target1/2/3 (30 days ago - in range), recent.txt (5 days ago - outside range). Expected count is 3.
metadata.verification_details: The evaluation checks that /tmp/file_count.txt exists and contains the value '3'. Setup creates 3 files modified 30 days ago (within 20-40 day range), 2 files at 50 days ago (outside range), and 1 file at 5 days ago (outside range). Only the 3 target files should be counted.
